label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's the letter, ready to copy and paste. I've kept it warm and a bit tired-sounding rather than polished, and used formatting that survives being pasted into WhatsApp.

---

**Hi everyone**

Thank you. Honestly, thank you.

My phone has been going mad since Saturday night and I've been reading messages on the bathroom floor at my sister's house in Rondebosch, crying at most of them, and I still haven't managed to answer anyone properly. So this letter is me trying to answer everybody at once. If you're the person who messaged me three times, I'm sorry. I'm reading them. I'll get to them.

Short version: **I'm safe. Marmalade is safe. Everyone in our building got out. Nobody was seriously hurt.**

**WHAT HAPPENED**

The fire started at around 11:40pm on Saturday night, 7 November, in a ground floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory. Not my flat. I'm on the second floor.

I was asleep. Uncle Faizel came knocking on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers — that is literally what woke me up, and bless that man, because I still don't know how I would have heard the smoke alarm over the fan. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade and nothing else. No bag, no documents, no laptop, no "important things" in the world. Just the two of us.

All 14 flats got out. Two people were treated for smoke at Groote Schuur and sent home the same night. The fire department said it was probably an electrical fault, but they're still investigating, so I'm not going to guess — I'll just tell you what they told me and leave it there.

Marmalade hid under the car for two hours afterwards. She eventually came out, extremely cross and extremely herself. She's currently sitting on my sister's pillow as if she pays rent here, which she does not, but she has made her feelings known.

**MY FLAT**

Smoke and water damage everywhere. The ceiling came down in the lounge. My landlord says nobody goes back in for at least six weeks, so right now "home" is a storage unit and a very generous sister in Rondebosch.

The thing that actually made me cry — and I promise this is not a bid for sympathy — is the end-of-year concert stuff I took home to laminate. All 22 crowns and the kids' handprint banner. Gone. I keep thinking about the banner especially, because it was covered in tiny handprints and nobody in that class could hold a glue stick properly, so it took me three hours.

Anyway. That's the short version. I don't want to relive it all, so that's all I'm going to write about the fire itself.

**THE FUNDRAISER**

Zinhle set up a BackaBuddy page for me. Target is R25 000 and we're at R11 400 this morning, which still doesn't feel real.

👉 **backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

If you'd rather give to something else that helps other people, please do that instead — and please do it through a page you trust, not through a bank account number someone sent you.

**⚠️ PLEASE DON'T SEND MONEY TO "THANDI FIRE RELIEF"**

I need everybody who forwards this to pass this part on:

There is a page going around called **"Thandi Fire Relief"** on some fundraising site, and there's also a WhatsApp message doing the rounds asking people to EFT to a Capitec account. **That is not me. That is not anyone helping me.** I have reported it, but reporting is slow and the message keeps spreading, so please warn people.

The only legitimate way to give is the BackaBuddy link above. No EFT to a bank account. No money to a "collector" who comes to your gate. Nothing sent to a link you found by searching my name — please check the address character by character, that's exactly how these things get set up.

If you've already paid money into that "fund", please tell me. It doesn't make you silly at all, these messages are very convincing. I'll help you work out how to report it and get it back.

And to be completely honest, because I know some of you are wondering: **I did not ask for money.** I hate it. I hate asking for help with anything, ever, and this felt awful. Zinhle said shut up and accept it, so I'm accepting it. But if all you can do is send a message, or bring me something, or just check in — that is genuinely enough, and I mean that.

**WHAT I ACTUALLY NEED**

1. **Help with a deposit for a new place.** This is the big one. If you know of a flat, a granny flat, a cottage, a space — anything — please tell me. This is what would help me most.
2. **School shoes and work clothes, size 6 / size 34.** Just the essentials. Shoes I can wear to school and clothes I can wear to school. That's it.
3. **A laptop.** An old one that still works would be perfect. All my lesson planning was on mine and it's gone. I can plan on paper, but I'd rather have something I can actually work on.

**WHAT I DON'T NEED** (please, I mean this)

- **More clothes.** I already have too many, thanks to some very kind people, and I'm going to pass the extras on to the other flats in our building who lost more than I did. A bag of lovely things arrived at my sister's gate at 7am on Sunday morning and I want to say — I saw it, and thank you, and it's going straight to the neighbours. If you were worried that it came across rude that I didn't come out of the house, please don't. You left it on the gate and I was asleep and it was exactly what I needed to find when I woke up.
- **Food.** My sister's freezer is full and she is cooking enough for a small army. Please don't bring food. Genuinely.

**FOR THE SCHOOL FAMILIES**

A few things so you're not left guessing:

- **The concert on 27 November is still happening.** Don't worry. The Ladybirds will have crowns. I'm sorting it and I promise it will be lovely.
- **I'm back at school on Wednesday.** Please don't make a big thing of it in front of the children. Just carry on as normal and treat me exactly like the same slightly tired teacher you always get.
- If your child asks why my hair looks a bit odd, or why I smell faintly of smoke, or why I'm not doing the usual music lesson properly — the answer is "Thandi had a bit of an adventure and she's fine", and that she can ask me about it on Wednesday. Honestly, that's the conversation I'd rather have. Please don't explain it for me in a way that makes it bigger than it is.

**ABOUT MESSAGES**

I'm going to be slow. I've got a few hundred of them and my battery and my brain are both giving up on me. Please don't be offended if I don't answer a DM for a few days, or if my reply is three words long. I am reading them. I am so grateful for every single one — I've cried at enough of them to fill a swimming pool.

But if you have something **practical** — a laptop, a place to rent, a pair of size 6 school shoes, a bag of groceries you were going to deliver anyway — that is the kind of message I will answer first, and I will answer it properly.

One more thing. Somebody said to me on Sunday that the good thing about a fire is you find out who your real friends are. And I want to say: I already knew. I just didn't know how loudly you all loved me. So thank you. For the messages, for the crying, for Uncle Faizel in his vest and slippers, for Zinhle being bossy at me, for my sister, for the mum who left a bag on a gate in the dark, for everyone who drove past on Sunday morning to look at the building and didn't drive past.

Furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can't.

With all my heart,
**Thandi**
*(Kindergarten teacher, Little Acorns Pre-Primary, Mowbray)*

---

**Two small notes from me:**

- I left out your flat number, even though it's in your notes — since the letter names the building and the fundraiser link, the unit number is the only thing standing between a scam page and your front door. Say the word if you'd rather I put it back in.
- I didn't put a year on the date (7 November was a Saturday this year), and I kept "back at school on Wednesday" as-is. If the letter is still going out by then, you may want to change that line to a date.
